blocks.body:
## Technical summary

Both rankers were effectively chance-like out of sample. The initial design used a static three-bar hold, one purged split, a two-tail portfolio, ReLU-era architecture assumptions, and full LightGBM lists without truncation. The economic result did not justify the fit complexity.

## Optimization evidence

Every phase now uses the same three diagnostics: LambdaRank training loss, LambdaRank validation loss, and LambdaRank validation NDCG. Epoch counts may differ across phases because early stopping and final training duration are part of the observed evidence.

## Economic evidence

The cumulative-return panel compares the strategy evidence with SPY and an equal-weight sector basket on a common 0% starting basis. Sharpe is shown separately because path quality and ending return answer different questions.

## Scope, metrics, and model specification

A query is one date across the 11 sectors. Pairwise accuracy is the share of correctly ordered within-date pairs; 50% is chance-like. NDCG rewards correct placement near the selected tail. Sharpe uses a zero risk-free rate.

## Model comparison

The evidence column prevents an observed test result from being read as equivalent to a validation-only WFO selection statistic.

## Limitations and robustness

The static-hold backtest is a clean reconstruction from the preserved data and parameter history, not byte-for-byte recovery of the original stop-based HTML. Phase 1 Sharpe uses non-overlapping three-bar cohorts and 252/3 annualization.

## Recommended next step

Keep this phase frozen as evidence. New tuning should use a new experiment identity, validation/WFO-only selection, and one final untouched-test evaluation.

## Further questions

- Does the long-only edge persist after costs and borrow-neutral constraints?
- How sensitive is the selected configuration to the sector sample and start date?
- Can one final test run reproduce the WFO-selected tree result without reopening model selection?
